name: Toughness (Solid White)
verdict: Same cubes at 9.2 s, left standing before washing: the smallest openings closed up, the upright cube came out straight and hard off the printer. Basis for the 0.05 mm profile at 9.2 s, with coupons at 12.4 and 7.8 s both fine.

tests.txt: Bars 5.0-19.8 s, after a first round centred on 9.2 s left a doughy surface. From 8.7 s the bars formed, thickness grew to 0.37 mm at 16.7 s and then stopped. Thin bars curl for a while after washing and flatten again as they dry. 12.4 s (0.30 mm) is the lowest bar with a dry surface and sharp pixels - deeper than the black bottle at the same time.
The coupon at 12.4 s, the exposure from the strips. Printed well.
The same coupon at 0.10 mm, 14 s. It printed fine.

The same cubes at 9.2 s, the exposure chosen for the 0.05 mm profile: the upright cube comes out straight, at 7.8 s it leans. Left standing before washing, so the smallest openings closed up as described below. The coupon is fine at both 12.4 and 7.8 s, so 9.2 s sits safely between them. Photo: the 12.4 s print, which came out the same, also left standing.

Two 14.5 mm lattice cubes. Washed straight after printing, the lattice stays open. Left standing, even for a few minutes, resin trapped in the smallest openings (0.25-0.5 mm on flat faces) hardens and closes them - the plugs come out shinier than the surface, so they cure after the print, not during it. The black bottle does not do this. Lowering the exposure did not help; 9.2 s is the lowest time that keeps the upright cube straight, at 7.8 s it leans. Hard straight off the printer. Photo: 7.8 s, washed within minutes.
The coupon at 0.10 mm, 12.4 s - the 0.05 mm time scaled by the same ratio as the black bottle. Printed fine, so the 14 s tried first is not needed.

Bend strips from 0.4 to 1.5 mm at 9.2 s, each bent back and forth about five times, 17 hours after printing. None broke: the thin strips flex and stay bent instead of snapping, while the thick base plate barely bends at all. Firm rather than brittle - fine details on figurines survive handling, and larger parts stay stiff and take knocks.
